title: Integral positive adjoint matrices and the simple-root strings
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring and $(G,T=D_A(M),\Phi,\Phi^\vee,\{a,b\},(X_a,X_b))$ a pinned split realization [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Use the canonical root exponentials and $n_a,n_b$ of [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus]. Suppose that the positive roots in the ordered basis $(a,b)$ are respectively $a,b$ (type $A_1\times A_1$), $a,b,c=a+b$ (type $A_2$), $a,b,c=a+b,d=2a+b$ (type $B_2$), or $a,b,c=a+b,d=2a+b,e=3a+b,f=3a+2b$ (type $G_2$), with $a$ short in the last two cases. Define $X_c=\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)X_a$ whenever $c$ occurs, $X_d=\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_b$ in $B_2$, and in $G_2$ define $X_d=\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_c$, $X_e=-\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_b$, $X_f=\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)X_e$.

Define an explicit free abelian group $L$ with basis $E_r$ indexed by these positive roots and the following alternating bilinear bracket, all unlisted brackets between different basis vectors being zero:
$$\begin{array}{c|l} A_1\times A_1&0\\ A_2&[E_a,E_b]=-E_c\\ B_2&[E_a,E_b]=-E_c,\ [E_a,E_c]=-2E_d\\ G_2&[E_a,E_b]=-E_c,\ [E_a,E_c]=-2E_d,\ [E_a,E_d]=-3E_e,\ [E_b,E_e]=E_f,\ [E_c,E_d]=-3E_f.\end{array}$$
For a positive root $r$ let $D_r$ be the integer matrix $v\mapsto[E_r,v]$. The rational polynomial matrix
$$P_r(z)=\sum_{j\geq0}\frac{z^jD_r^j}{j!}$$
is finite and has coefficients in $\mathbf Z[z]$. For every commutative $A$-algebra $R$, the map $E_r\mapsto X_r$ identifies $L\otimes_{\mathbf Z}R$ with $\bigoplus_{r\in\Phi^+}R\otimes_A\mathfrak g_r$ and identifies $P_r(z)$ with the restriction of $\operatorname{Ad}(\exp_r(zX_r))$ to this module, for all $z\in R$. The bracket on the latter module is the differential commutator bracket: $[U,V]$ is the coefficient of $\epsilon\eta$ in $U(\epsilon)V(\eta)U(-\epsilon)V(-\eta)$ over $R[\epsilon,\eta]/(\epsilon^2,\eta^2)$, where $U(\epsilon)$ denotes the dual-number tangent point. Thus the displayed bracket also agrees with this bracket under the identification.

There is in addition the following integral string description. For either ordered choice $(\alpha,\beta)=(a,b)$ or $(b,a)$ let $q$ be the largest nonnegative integer with $\beta+q\alpha\in\Phi$. There are generators $V_i\in\mathfrak g_{\beta+i\alpha}$, $0\leq i\leq q$, with $V_0=X_\beta$ and, after every algebra extension,
$$[X_\alpha,V_i]=(i+1)V_{i+1}\quad(0\leq i<q),\qquad \operatorname{Ad}(n_\alpha)V_i=(-1)^i V_{q-i}.$$
All identifications and formulas commute with arbitrary base change, including characteristics $2$ and $3$. The matrices $P_r$ are formed over $\mathbf Q$ and proved integral before evaluation; this is not division in $R$.

proof.text: Write $x_r(z)=\exp_r(zX_r)$. First make the tangent conventions explicit. In the associative convolution algebra of [lem-sfb-convolution-linear-map-algebra] for the coordinate coalgebra of $G$, a tangent point is $1+\epsilon u$, its inverse is $1-\epsilon u$, and their four-factor commutator is $1+\epsilon\eta(u*v-v*u)$. Thus the bracket in the statement is alternating and satisfies Jacobi, by expanding the associative commutators; conjugation preserves it, and the coefficient of $z$ in $\operatorname{Ad}(x_r(z))v$ is $[X_r,v]$. Full-torus equivariance in [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] implies that its coefficient of $z^j$, for $v\in\mathfrak g_s$, has weight $s+jr$: compare the independent monomials $e_m$ in $A[M]$. Hence a bracket is zero if its weight is not a root or zero, and every conjugation coefficient of such a weight vanishes. These coefficient arguments work over polynomial test algebras, not just field-valued points.

source.place: Agent tangent calculation accompanying Section 6.2, Steps 2--3; associative convolution expansion and full-character coefficient comparison.

proof.text: For either simple root $\alpha$, form $H=Z_G(\ker\chi_{\alpha_0})$, where $\alpha_0$ generates the saturated rank-one sublattice containing $\alpha$. By [lem-sfb-relative-root-rank-one-centralizer], $H$ is reductive with just the root modules $\mathfrak g_{\pm\alpha}$ and the same torus. Its two modules are free on the pinning vector and its linked opposite vector, by [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus]. Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-framed-noetherian-descent] to this rank-one framed group, then [lem-sfb-relative-rank-one-local-matrix-model] to its Noetherian model. Pull back the affine open cover to $A$. On each open $\operatorname{Spec}C$ this identifies $H$ with a central split torus times $\operatorname{SL}_2$, $\operatorname{PGL}_2$ or $\operatorname{GL}_2$, with $\alpha$ the ratio character. If $X_\alpha=cE_{12}$, where $c\in C^\times$, the map $g\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(c,1)g\operatorname{diag}(c^{-1},1)$ in the matrix factor (followed by the quotient for $\operatorname{PGL}_2$) is a homomorphism $\operatorname{SL}_{2,C}\to H_C\subseteq G_C$.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.8 and rank-one local matrix reduction; explicit pinning normalization. This is a local calculation, not an appeal to rank-two classification.

proof.text: The local upper and lower maps are $I+zcE_{12}$ and $I+zc^{-1}E_{21}$. The uniqueness and linkage assertions of [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] identify them with the given root exponentials, and identify the image of $w=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with $n_\alpha$. The diagonal image is $\alpha^\vee$: its geometric fibres are the canonical coroot, and [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality] upgrades this equality to equality of the split-torus morphisms over $C$. Restrict the adjoint representation to any full $\alpha$-string $\beta,\ldots,\beta+q\alpha$ independent of $\alpha$. Step 1 makes the sum of these root lines stable under the upper and lower groups and the diagonal. The determinant-one matrix charts with a unit in the first row admit Gaussian elimination; these two charts cover because that row is unimodular. Thus they give a restricted representation on this sum. In the cases used below the listed root sets give $\langle\beta,\alpha^\vee\rangle=-q$, so the diagonal weights are $-q,-q+2,\ldots,q$. The lower group fixes $X_\beta$, since $\beta-j\alpha$ is absent for $j>0$. We may therefore apply [lem-sfb-sl2-integral-orbit-coefficients] to this local representation. Its coefficient vectors are the coefficients of the globally defined root-subgroup orbit, so its polynomial identities agree on overlaps and hold over $A$.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.9, local rank-one matrices, and agent integral orbit-coefficient calculation; the root pairings are read directly from the four given lists.

proof.text: If the type is not $A_1\times A_1$, the $b$-string through $a$ has length one. Its orbit coefficients are $X_a,\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)X_a=X_c$, so $[X_b,X_a]=X_c$. Now apply [lem-sfb-sl2-integral-orbit-coefficients] to the $a$-string through $b$. Its coefficients $V_i$ satisfy $V_0=X_b$, $V_1=[X_a,X_b]=-X_c$, and $\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)V_i=(-1)^iV_{q-i}$. For $A_2$, $q=1$ and $V_1=-X_c$. For $B_2$, $q=2$ and $V_2=\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_b=X_d$. For $G_2$, $q=3$, $V_3=\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)X_b=-X_e$, and $-V_2=\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)V_1=-X_d$, hence $V_2=X_d$. Each vector is a generator by its defining Weyl transport; no integer is cancelled to show this. The linear coefficient identity gives $[X_a,V_i]=(i+1)V_{i+1}$. The reversed ordered simple-root pair uses the length-one $b$-string already computed. In $A_1\times A_1$ both strings have length zero and the same lemma gives the asserted formulas with $V_0=X_\beta$. This proves the whole string clause with its specified signs.

source.place: Section 6.2, Step 2 and Example 6.2.9: signed Weyl vectors; agent assembly from the rank-one coefficient identities.

proof.text:
The previous step gives $[X_a,X_b]=-X_c$, and, when present, $[X_a,X_c]=-2X_d$ and $[X_a,X_d]=-3X_e$. In $G_2$ the $b$-string through $e$ has length one; its top vector is $\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)X_e=X_f$, so the same coefficient identity gives $[X_b,X_e]=X_f$. Jacobi from step 1 then gives
$$[X_c,X_d]=[[X_b,X_a],X_d]=[X_b,[X_a,X_d]]-[X_a,[X_b,X_d]]=-3X_f,$$
since $b+d$ is not a root. All other brackets between different positive basis vectors vanish by step 1 and the displayed root lists. Alternation gives the reverse ordered brackets and the diagonal brackets are zero. Thus the complete displayed integral bracket table is established, including its differential-commutator interpretation.

source.place: Agent calculation from the signed strings of Example 6.2.9 and the root lists of Section 6.2, Step 2; Jacobi is expanded in step 1.

proof.text:
The upper-orbit formulas of [lem-sfb-sl2-integral-orbit-coefficients] now compute the simple-root actions. In the following lists write $r$ for $X_r$, put $z$ for the root parameter, and omit every basis vector fixed by the action. For $A_2$:
$$\operatorname{Ad}(x_a(z)):b\mapsto b-zc,\qquad \operatorname{Ad}(x_b(z)):a\mapsto a+zc.$$
For $B_2$:
$$\operatorname{Ad}(x_a(z)):b\mapsto b-zc+z^2d,\ c\mapsto c-2zd;\qquad \operatorname{Ad}(x_b(z)):a\mapsto a+zc.$$
For $G_2$:
$$\operatorname{Ad}(x_a(z)):b\mapsto b-zc+z^2d-z^3e,\ c\mapsto c-2zd+3z^2e,\ d\mapsto d-3ze;$$
$$\operatorname{Ad}(x_b(z)):a\mapsto a+zc,\ e\mapsto e+zf.$$
The length-one $b$-strings and the isolated length-zero string through $d$ also give
$$\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)a=c,\quad\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)c=-a,\quad\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)d=d,\quad\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)e=f,\quad\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)f=-e.$$
For $A_1\times A_1$ both positive-root actions are the identity. All omitted coefficients vanish by the full-torus support calculation in step 1.

source.place: Agent explicit binomial calculation, with normalization of Example 6.2.9; actual polynomial actions are computed before any rational exponential is used.

proof.text:
For a nonsimple positive root $r$, the only possible coefficient of degree greater than one on a positive root vector is in type $G_2$, for $r=c$ acting on $a$, with degree two and output $f$; this follows by enumerating $s+jr$ in the four lists. Every possible linear coefficient is already the bracket of step 5. For the exceptional quadratic coefficient, root-exponential uniqueness gives $x_c(z)=n_bx_a(z)n_b^{-1}$. Step 6 therefore computes
$$\operatorname{Ad}(x_c(z))a=\operatorname{Ad}(n_b)\operatorname{Ad}(x_a(z))(-c)=a+2zd-3z^2f.$$
Consequently the remaining nonidentity images are: $B_2$, $x_c(z):a\mapsto a+2zd$; $G_2$,
$$x_c(z):d\mapsto d-3zf,\qquad x_d(z):a\mapsto a+3ze,\ c\mapsto c+3zf,\qquad x_e(z):b\mapsto b-zf.$$
Here these denote adjoint actions, and all unspecified images are fixed. This proves every positive-root polynomial action, rather than recovering it from its differential in a ring where factorials might vanish.

source.place: Agent positive-root support enumeration and conjugation calculation; Example 6.2.9 normalization.

proof.text: Define the free group $L$ exactly as in the statement. Each $X_r$ is a generator of its root line, so $E_r\mapsto X_r$ gives the required isomorphism, and step 5 identifies its bracket. The nonzero powers of $D_r$ on the basis are read from that table: in $B_2$, $D_a^2E_b=2E_d$; in $G_2$, $D_a^2E_b=2E_d$, $D_a^3E_b=-6E_e$, $D_a^2E_c=6E_e$, and $D_c^2E_a=-6E_f$. All other powers of order at least two vanish. Thus $D_r^j/j!$ is integral, and the finite sums over $\mathbf Q$ give exactly the integer polynomial matrices of steps 6--7 (in $A_2$ all squares vanish). The comparison over $R$ is evaluation of these integer matrices, not division in $R$. The root-line and tangent comparisons in [lem-sfb-arbitrary-base-root-lines-coroots], and the base-change compatibility of the exponentials in [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus], identify every constructed vector and polynomial after any algebra extension. All calculations were polynomial or dual-number identities, so they include nonflat base changes, rings with nilpotents, characteristics two and three, and the zero test algebra.
